survey: A red British telephone box, seen from the front-left at three-quarter view. A dark grey plinth sits flat on the ground and the box stands squarely on it. Two faces are visible: the left side and the front door. Each has a red frame with a grid of small glazing bars, the classic K6 look, simplified. The front face is a door with a silver pull handle on its left edge, where the opening edge belongs. Inside, a grey payphone with a screen and keypad hangs on the back wall, seen through the door glass. Its handset rests in a cradle on the left of the unit, and a coiled cord runs down and back into the unit. At the top, a domed roof caps the box. Under the roof, each face has a white sign panel with a gold crown above it. The roof overhang and the sign panels match on both faces, and all edges meet cleanly at the corner posts. Nothing floats, nothing is missing or doubled, and the box could stand and work.
